headline: 6,000+ visitors
details: Palm Coast reported more than 6,000 visitors and advertised 13 food trucks. A large family crowd does not automatically mean low competition.
dessertCompetition: Historical/adjacent rosters included Kona Ice, Italian ice and other sweets.

headline: Dessert saturation mattered
details: The food court lineup included multiple sweet/frozen categories. Use the actual roster, not just headline attendance, when deciding whether a future slot is worth paying for.
dessertCompetition: Kona Ice, Andrea's Italian Ice, The Sugared Lemon, funnel cake and mini donuts were among the published sweet options.

headline: Demand existed — so did direct competition
details: City reporting described successful 2025 events, while a March lineup included frozen and sweet competitors.
dessertCompetition: Kona Ice, Sweet Melissa's Homemade Ice Cream, lemonade and other sweets were present in a historical lineup.

headline: Weather moved the whole event
details: The October 2025 edition was moved to February 2026. That makes refund, credit and rainout language commercially important before paying a future fee.
dessertCompetition: Request the current roster rather than relying on historic festival size claims.

headline: 649 runners / walkers
details: Local reporting counted a record 649 participants. That is a participant count, not a dessert-customer count.
dessertCompetition: Finish-area included food/after-party activity; confirm incumbent suppliers before pitching.

headline: $100 day, then $40 day
details: Scoops paid $75 per day for the location. The weak walk-up result is a useful warning against rent-only traffic experiments without a scheduled crowd.
dessertCompetition: Not the main issue. Traffic conversion and stop visibility were the bigger problems.

headline: Typical early summer days around $100–$120
details: Best early-summer day was around $200. Use these real Scoops numbers as a baseline when deciding whether an event fee and long service window make sense.
dessertCompetition: Location vending baseline, not a festival comparison.
